data.name: Connect_GuideTitle
data.value: Playing with friends over the internet

data.name: Connect_GuideIntro
data.value: Friends who aren't on your Wi-Fi can join through a virtual LAN tool. You and your friends join one network in it, and this tab then shows your address in that network. Any tool works, so pick the one your friends already use.

data.name: Connect_GuideStep1
data.value: 1. Install the same tool as your friends, turn it on, and create a network (or join the one a friend made).

data.name: Connect_GuideStep2
data.value: 2. On the Players tab here, add each friend's Minecraft name to the whitelist.

data.name: Connect_GuideStep3
data.value: 3. Start the server. A line for the tool appears at the top of this tab: press Copy and send that address to your friends.

data.name: Connect_GuideStep4
data.value: 4. Install the same tool, turn it on and join your network.

data.name: Connect_GuideStep5
data.value: 5. In Minecraft (the same version as the server) choose Multiplayer, then Add Server, paste the address into Server Address, then Done, and join.

data.name: Connect_GuideTools
data.value: Where to click in common tools

data.name: Connect_ToolRadmin
data.value: Radmin VPN (free): choose Network, then Create Network, with a name and a password of at least 6 characters. Friends choose Network, then Join Network. Addresses start with 26.

data.name: Connect_ToolZeroTier
data.value: ZeroTier (free): create a network at my.zerotier.com. Everyone joins it with its Network ID, then you tick each new member under Auth.

data.name: Connect_ToolTailscale
data.value: Tailscale (sign-in needed): sign in on your PC, then share your PC with each friend from the Tailscale admin console. Addresses start with 100.

data.name: Connect_ToolHamachi
data.value: Hamachi (free for up to 5 people): choose Network, then Create a new network. Friends choose Join an existing network. Addresses start with 25.

data.name: Connect_GuideNotListed
data.value: Your tool isn't listed at the top? Check that it's turned on and in a network, then press Refresh. A tool WaNut doesn't know shows under the name Windows gives its adapter.

data.name: Connect_GuideTrouble
data.value: Friends can't join? Check that they're on the whitelist, that Windows Firewall lets them in (above), and that everyone has the same Minecraft version. If the tool itself can't reach your PC (most have a Ping option), the problem is the tool's connection, not the server.
